stem:
Wafa constructs a six-petal flower with ruler and compass. Equal radii from the centre and equal $60^{\circ}$ turn angles are required before the outer petal arcs are traced.

Which plan is correct?

options.text: Equal radii and $60^{\circ}$ turns are names only, so the flower is finished with no support construction drawn.
Trace the outer petal arcs first, and add equal radii and $60^{\circ}$ turns afterwards.
Construct the equal radii and $60^{\circ}$ support angles first, then trace the outer petal arcs.
Tracing the outer petal arcs is what creates the equal radii and $60^{\circ}$ turn angles.

teacher.key_rationale: A ruler-and-compass flower is exact only after its support structure—equal radii and equal $60^{\circ}$ turns—is built. The visible petal arcs are traced after those constraints.
